original.target_description: Unassigned side; placeholder only, not examined.

replication.target_description: Giuliano et al. (2018), preschool children enrolled in Head Start; association of cumulative SES risk (income, maternal education, marital status) with mean frontocentral unattended-probe ERP amplitude, 150–200 ms post probe onset; Results, Hypothesis 1. Predictor differs from maternal educational attainment alone in supplied description.

n.sample_role: Children in the explicitly stated final analyses; preschool participants, not trials, electrodes, or observations pooled across children. Applies to the located cumulative-SES-risk correlation.
n.exclusions: EEG successfully obtained from 123 children; eight tested in Spanish excluded; among the remainder, 13 declined ECG electrodes, one had unusable impedance data, and one caregiver declined socioeconomic information. Task analysis required at least seven of 12 comprehension questions correct. ERP artifact-contaminated epochs were excluded. No further child exclusion count supplied for these criteria.
n.location: Method, Participants; auditory selective attention task and EEG sections
n.quote: Therefore, final analyses included 100 children (50 females) ranging in age from 3–5 years old ( M = 4.31, SD = .54, range = 3.18–5.37).

es.location: Results, Hypothesis 1: Early adversity impacts selective attention; corroborated by Table 2, SES risks × Unattended ERP amplitudes
es.quote: SES risk was positively associated with mean amplitude of ERPs elicited by unattended probes during the dichotic listening task [ r (98) = .21, p = .037], such that children with more risk factors showed a larger positive deflection in ERPs to distractor sounds.

p.location: Results, Hypothesis 1: Early adversity impacts selective attention, same r (98) = .21 test
p.quote: SES risk was positively associated with mean amplitude of ERPs elicited by unattended probes during the dichotic listening task [ r (98) = .21, p = .037], such that children with more risk factors showed a larger positive deflection in ERPs to distractor sounds.

notes: Identity independently checked: supplied cache identifies the exact title, all eight named authors, DOI 10.1037/dev0000499, and final publication Dev Psychol. 2018 Sep;54(9):1674–1686. Document is a PMC author manuscript with full Method, Results, Discussion and references, not an abstract-only excerpt or secondary account. No PDF was supplied; canonical text has no page markers, so section locations are used and the supplied p. 1679 cannot be visually verified. Target correspondence: the located test is cumulative SES risk versus unattended-probe ERP amplitude, not maternal educational attainment alone. Methods define cumulative risk using household income, maternal education and marital status. Discussion explicitly distinguishes the prior study’s maternal-education proxy from this study’s cumulative-risk framework. target_match=false records this known predictor difference; values describe the actual located conceptual replication test and must not be relabelled as a maternal-education-only correlation. N=100 is explicitly the final analysis sample, not inferred from r degrees of freedom. No N arithmetic or effect-size conversion performed. Results first mention age as a covariate in subsequent analyses, while Table 2 is explicitly zero-order and reproduces r=.21; the extracted statistic retains the authors’ r designation without reclassifying it as a partial correlation. Original and reported_success are unassigned placeholders.
